question: Como consultar os tipos de todas as colunas?
reference_facts: dtypes apresenta um tipo por coluna.

claims.text: Para consultar os tipos de todas as colunas de um DataFrame, use a propriedade `dtypes`, que retorna uma Series com o tipo de dados de cada coluna. Exemplo: `df.dtypes`.

evidence_quotes.quote:
_property_ DataFrame.dtypes [[source]](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/v2.2.3/pandas/core/generic.py#L6432-L6461)

Return the dtypes in the DataFrame.

This returns a Series with the data type of each column.
The result’s index is the original DataFrame’s columns. Columns
with mixed types are stored with the `object` dtype. See
the User Guide for more.

Returns:pandas.Series

The data type of each column.

sources.title: conversion of dtypes
sources.text:
To see all the child dtypes of a generic `dtype` like `numpy.number` you
can define a function that returns a tree of child dtypes:

```
In [441]: def subdtypes(dtype):
   .....:     subs = dtype.__subclasses__()
   .....:     if not subs:
   .....:         return dtype
   .....:     return [dtype, [subdtypes(dt) for dt in subs]]
   .....:
```

All NumPy dtypes are subclasses of `numpy.generic`:

sources.title: or absolute, starting with a slash:\
sources.text:
\
As an alternative to converters, the type for an entire column can\
be specified using the `dtype` keyword, which takes a dictionary\
mapping column names to types. To interpret data with\
no type inference, use the type `str` or `object`.\
\
```\
pd.read_excel("path_to_file.xls", dtype={"MyInts": "int64", "MyText": str})\
```\
